4. Upon hearing the parties and considering the materials on record, the trial Court, by its judgment and decree dated 25.07.2011, dismissed the suit. The plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No.222 of 2011 which was dismissed. Then he filed civil revisional application in the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which was madeabsolute. Thus, the defendant No.1 has preferred this appeal upon getting leave. 

 5. Mr. Md. Mostafa Neaz Ahmed, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that the trial Court as well as appellate Court concurrently found that the agreement, in question, is agreement for loan and the same was not an agreement to sell the suit land, the High Court Division has committed erred in law in decreeing the suit for specific performance of contract treating the same as an agreement to sell. He further submits that the defendant appellant received a sum of tk.1,00,000/- from his brother as per the decision of the family members, which does not constitute an agreement to sell his property. 

 7. It is the settled principle that the relief of specific performance is discretionary but such discretion must be exercised in accordance with sound and reasonable judicial principles not arbitrarily. The Court is not bound to grant specific performance merely because it lawful to do so. The motive behind the litigation should also enter into. In order to enable a Court to decree specific performance of a contract, the terms of the contract must be clear, definite, certain and complete. In the pleading the plaintiff has, inter alia, stated, “অতঃপর ১নং বিবাদী মোঃ আলী আকরাম হোসেন (বাচ্চু) তাহার আর্থিক অস্বচ্ছলতার কারনে দোকান ঘর তাহার ছোট ভ্রাতা মোঃ রহমানের বরাবরে নামায় জিদ্বা রাখিয়া গত ইং ২৫/৭/৯৭ তারিখে ১,০০,০০০/- (এক লক্ষ) টাকা ধার হিসাবে গ্রহণ করে। উক্ত ১,০০,০০০/- (এক লক্ষ) টাকা ১নং বিবাদী ৩ বছরের মধ্যে বাদীকে ফেরত প্রদান করার মর্মে তপশীল বর্নিত জমি ও তদুপরি দোকান ঘর বাদীর বরাবর তিন বছরের জন্য জিম্বা রাখে । যদি তিন বছরের মধ্যে ১নং বিবাদী উক্ত ১,০০১০০০/- টাকা বাদীর বরাবরে ফেরত প্রদান করিতে ব্যর্থ হয় তাহা হইলে নাঃ সম্পত্তি বাদীর বরাবরে রেজিঃ খাস কবলা দলিল করিয়া দিতে বাধ্য থাকিবে। In support his pleading the plaintiff as P.W.1 has 3810, ১নং বিবাদী আমার বড় ভাই। ২৫/৭/১৯৯৭ইং তারিখে ১নং বিবাদী নাদ জমি আমার একটি জিম্মায় রেখে আমার নিকট থেকে ১,০০,০০০/- এক লক্ষ টাকা গ্রহন করে। শর্ত ছিল যে তিন বছরের মধ্যে ১নং বিবাদী আমাকে টাকা ফেরত দিবে । আমার টাকা ফেরত প্রদানে ব্যার্থ হলে তার জমি আমার বরাবরে রেজিঃ করিয়া দিবে। এই জন্য ২৮/৭/৯৭ ইং তারিখে ১নং বিবাদী আমার বরাবরে লিখিত বায়না চুক্তিনামা সম্পাদন করিয়া দেয়।” 

 8. In action for specific performance plaintiff should prove existence of concluded contract between himself and defendant and that he was ready and willing at all material dates to perform his part of contract. On perusal of the alleged agreement to sell, pleading and evidence of P.W.1, it appears that the plaintiff has admitted that the defendant appellant had taken loan of a sum of tk.1,00,000/-from his brother, the plain-tiff. It has been stated that the defendant No.1 mortgaged the scheduled property against that loan amount. It was further stated that in case of failure of payment of loan, the defendant No.1 would exe-cute sale deed in favour of the plaintiff. An agreement for loan can not be any away termed as agreement to sell since the defendant No.1 had no intention to sell his property. It further appears that there is no statement in the said agreement regarding the fixation of consideration of the scheduled property and payment of the earnest money. It cannot be taken to be an agreement to sell within the meaning of section 53-A spelling out the terms of an agreement for sale. In order to pass a decree in a suit for specific performance of contract following matters should be looked into: (i) the express terms of the agreement; (ii) nature of the property; (iii) surrounding circumstances; (iv) intention of the parties and (v) reciprocal promise of executing, sale deed. There is no averment in the pleading as to the offer and acceptance or refusal to accept the consideration which are the criteria to get a decree for specific performance of contract, the High Court Division most illegally treated the alleged agreement as an agreement for sale and, thereby, erroneously set aside the judgment and decree of the courts of facts below. This was not a fit case in which specific performance of contract should be enforced by the Court.
